_comment: correctOptionId and explanation are only ever returned by POST /api/quiz/:bodyId/answer. Keys starting with _ are ignored by the API.

options.text: It is covered in hot lava
Its dust and rocks contain rusty iron
It reflects red light from the Sun
Its sky is full of red clouds

questions.explanation: Martian dust is rich in iron oxide, the same stuff as rust, which gives the planet its reddish colour.

questions.prompt: What did the Ingenuity helicopter do first in history?

options.text: Landed on Mars without a parachute
Carried an astronaut across a crater
Made a powered, controlled flight on another planet
Flew all the way from Earth to Mars

questions.explanation: On 19 April 2021 Ingenuity lifted off, hovered and landed, the first powered, controlled flight on a world beyond Earth.

questions.prompt: In which crater did the Perseverance rover land in 2021?
questions.explanation: Perseverance landed in Jezero Crater, which once held a lake and a river delta: a good place to look for signs of ancient life.

questions.prompt: What did the InSight lander's seismometer measure?
questions.explanation: InSight recorded more than 1,300 marsquakes. The way their waves travelled revealed the planet's crust, mantle and core.

questions.prompt: Where does the Curiosity rover get its electricity?

options.text: Batteries charged by the Ingenuity helicopter

questions.explanation: Curiosity carries a radioisotope power system that turns the heat of decaying plutonium into electricity, so it keeps working at night and in dust storms.

questions.prompt: What was the name of the lunar module that landed the first people on the Moon in 1969?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed in the lunar module Eagle on 20 July 1969. Columbia was the command module that stayed in orbit.

questions.prompt: How strong is gravity on the Moon compared with Earth?

options.text: There is no gravity at all

questions.explanation: The Moon's surface gravity is about one-sixth of Earth's, which is why astronauts could take long, bouncing steps.

questions.prompt: Which Apollo missions took a Lunar Roving Vehicle to the Moon?
questions.explanation: The rover flew on the last three Apollo missions, 15, 16 and 17, letting astronauts travel many kilometres from their lander.

questions.prompt: What do scientists use the retroreflectors left on the Moon for?

options.text: Lighting up the Moon at night
Melting ice at the lunar poles
Bouncing lasers back to measure the distance to the Moon

questions.explanation: Observatories fire laser pulses at the mirrors and time the round trip, which shows the Moon is moving away by about 3.8 cm a year.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the small rover carried by the Chandrayaan-3 Vikram lander?
questions.explanation: Vikram released the six-wheeled Pragyan rover after landing near the Moon's south pole in August 2023.
